label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to high school teacher Walter Shirley and his wife Bertha. After an orphan childhood, she arrived at Green Gables, where Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert mistakenly received her instead of the boy they had requested. Though initially facing the prospect of being sent away or given to Mrs. Blewett, she was allowed to stay. Soon after arriving in Avonlea, she formed a close friendship with Diana Barry and developed a intense rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he called her "Carrots." She attended Avonlea school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy, joining the Queen's preparation class. She excelled academically, winning the Avery scholarship at Queen's Academy. Upon completing her studies, she chose to forego college to remain at Green Gables, taking up a teaching position at Avonlea School and serving as secretary for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye comes to Avonlea
unit: Anthony Pye comes to Avonlea to live with his aunt, Mrs. George Pye, as an orphan nephew and begins attending the local school under Anne Shirley's instruction. Holding a prejudice that female teachers are useless, he behaves with constant scorn, insolence, and quiet defiance. He causes various misdeeds in the classroom, such as pouring slate water down Aurelia Clay's neck and planting a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer. When caught putting the mouse in the drawer, he admits to it insolently, prompting Anne to whip him with a heavy hardwood pointer. To Anne's surprise, the whipping earns his respect; the following day, he politely offers to carry her books to school and praises her discipline as being as effective as a male teacher's. When Anne later resigns her teaching post, he fights two pitched battles with other boys to process his feelings about her departure.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews is a young man.
unit: Billy Andrews is a young man living in Avonlea with his family. When a concert was held at the White Sands Hotel, Billy drove a double-seated buggy to transport his sister Jane, Anne Shirley, and Diana Barry to the venue. Insisting that Anne ride on the front seat beside him, he was puffed up with pride to drive her, though he remained mostly silent, offering only grins and chuckles to her conversation. After the performance, he decamped to wait outside with his team in mortal fear of being invited inside for supper. He successfully drove the girls back home after the event.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman was hired by Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Leonora Bowman was hired by Miss Lavendar Lewis to live at Echo Lodge for board and clothes, serving as her handmaid. Because her three older sisters—Charlotta, Julietta, and Evelina—had previously served in the same position and looked remarkably alike, Miss Lavendar dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth.' She welcomed Anne Shirley and Diana Barry when they accidentally arrived at Echo Lodge for tea, delighting in demonstrating the local echoes. Over time, she grew deeply concerned about Miss Lavendar's failing spirits and health, confiding her worries to Anne during a berry-picking trip. When Stephen Irving returned to court Miss Lavendar, Charlotta anxious watched the courtship unfold alongside Anne. Following Miss Lavendar's wedding to Stephen Irving, Charlotta helped clean and pack up Echo Lodge, preparing to move to Boston in the autumn to continue living with the newlyweds.

value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were left orphans upon the death of their mother, Mary Keith. Because Mary was a third cousin to Marilla Cuthbert's late relative, Marilla brought the children to Green Gables to live. From the moment he arrived, Davy proved to be a constant handful, indulging in endless physical activity, snatching cake, and playing pranks. Within his first few days, he dropped a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, coaxed his sister into falling into a pigpen, and placed a toad in Marilla's bed. Under Anne Shirley's gentle and understanding guidance, Davy gradually began learning moral lessons against lying, stealing jam, and disobeying rules, though he frequently lapsed into accidental mischief. He started attending Avonlea School alongside his sister, sitting with Milty Boulter and joining in schoolboy squabbles and games. Following the death of his uncle Richard Keith, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora, securing their permanent home at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Diana meets Anne Shirley
unit: Diana meets Anne Shirley when Anne moves to Green Gables, and the two rapidly become inseparable bosom friends, swearing an oath of lifelong devotion in the garden. They share many childhood adventures, including creating playhouses like Idlewild, starting a story club, and exploring local spots. After accidentally drinking three glasses of currant wine at Green Gables thinking it was raspberry cordial, Diana becomes ill, leading her strict mother to briefly forbid them from playing together; however, Mrs. Barry relents after Anne helps nurse Minnie May through a severe bout of croup. Diana participates in various local escapades, such as accidentally leaping onto Great-Aunt Josephine Barry in the spare-room bed during a sleepover, which surprisingly earns Aunt Josephine's affection and musical sponsorship. Although Diana does not join the Queen's class due to her parents' decision not to send her to college, she remains Anne's closest companion and joins the Avonlea Improvement Society. In her mid-teens, she enters a romantic courtship with Fred Wright.

label: History
value: Dora's mother died while sick.
unit: Following her sick mother's death, Dora and her twin brother Davy were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert to live at Green Gables. During her first week there, Davy coaxed her onto a pigpen fence, causing her to fall in, and subsequently drenched her with pump water under the pretense of washing her dress. Shortly after, Davy tricked her and locked her inside Mr. Harrison's toolhouse, leaving her frightened and cold until Anne Shirley found her. When autumn arrived, she began attending school with Anne as her teacher, sitting with Mirabel Cotton and getting frightened by Mirabel's tales of a deceased walking uncle. She survived a terrifying hailstorm at Green Gables by calmly holding Anne's hand and praying. After her uncle Richard Keith passed away, leaving a monetary inheritance for her maintenance, Marilla and Anne decided to keep her permanently.

value: > Anne, look here. Can’t we be good friends? I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair that time. I didn’t mean to vex you and I only meant it for a joke. Besides, it’s so long ago. I think your hair is awfully pretty now—honest I do. Let’s be friends.

value: > It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?

label: History
value: In April, Mr. Harrison bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island
unit: In April, Mr. Harrison bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, moving from New Brunswick. He initially gained a reputation as a eccentric bachelor, keeping irregular meal hours, leaving dishes unwashed, and keeping a swearing parrot named Ginger. He got into a heated dispute with Anne Shirley after her Jersey cow broke into his oatfield, but when Anne accidentally sold his cow and came to apologize, he quickly forgave her and accepted a homemade cake as a peace offering. The two soon developed a warm friendship, frequently visiting each other across the fields. When a lightning strike hit his house and killed Ginger, Anne went over to comfort him in his grief. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife Emily arrived in Avonlea after seeing a newspaper note, and the two reconciled and resumed married life together.

unit: In April, Mr. Harrison bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, moving from New Brunswick. He initially gained a reputation as a eccentric bachelor, keeping irregular meal hours, leaving dishes unwashed, and keeping a swearing parrot named Ginger. He got into a heated dispute with Anne Shirley after her Jersey cow broke into his oatfield, but when Anne accidentally sold his cow and came to apologize, he quickly forgave her and accepted a homemade cake as a peace offering. The two soon developed a warm friendship, frequently visiting each other across the fields. When a lightning strike hit his house and killed Ginger, Anne went over to comfort him in his grief. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife Emily arrived in Avonlea after seeing a newspaper note, and the two reconciled and resumed married life together.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of the Andrews family and attended the local school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy. She joined Anne Shirley's story club, though she preferred writing sensible stories without romance. Jane joined the Queen's class, passed her Entrance examination calmly, and completed her studies at Queen's Academy, earning honors in domestic science. After graduating, she accepted a position as a teacher in Newbridge, where she maintained order strictly and earned a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. She active participated in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving on fundraising and petition committees. After her successful term at Newbridge, she was tipped to take over the school in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Josie attended Avonlea school.
unit: Josie attended Avonlea school, where she frequently cheated and engaged in rivalries with her classmates. She defied Anne Shirley by walking the Barrys' board fence and then dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Josie participated in school events, sulking when denied the role of Fairy Queen in a concert dialogue, and later won first prize for knitted lace at an exhibition. She joined the Queen's class organized by Miss Stacy and scraped through the entrance examinations by three marks. While attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, she earned a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student and boarder who frequented outings with Frank Stockley. After completing her first year at Queen's, she decided to return to the Academy for another year rather than teach.

The couple married the following August in her garden at Echo Lodge and departed for a wedding trip to the Pacific coast, planning to reside in Boston while returning to Echo Lodge each summer.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla. When he was sixty, they decided to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work, but due to a miscommunicated message, an eleven-year-old girl named Anne Shirley arrived at Bright River station instead. Driving her home to Green Gables, Matthew was quickly won over by her lively chatter and persuaded Marilla to keep her. He grew deeply attached to Anne, frequently indulging her and taking pride in her academic successes. Struggling with failing health, Matthew suffered a fatal heart attack after reading news of the Abbey Bank's failure, which wiped out his and Marilla's savings. He was buried in Avonlea, where Anne continued to visit his grave regularly to honor his memory.

label: History
value: Paul Irving moved from the United States
unit: Paul Irving moved from the United States to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, in Avonlea. Upon entering Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized his poetic nature and imagination. He invented imaginary characters known as his 'rock people' and shared his thoughts with Anne. After hearing Anne praise Paul, Davy Keith was inspired to improve his own habits. Anne later introduced Paul to Miss Lavendar Lewis, with whom he instantly connected over shared romantic fancies. After Paul wrote to his father about visiting Miss Lavendar, Stephen Irving came to Avonlea, reunited with Miss Lavendar, and married her. Following the wedding, Paul prepared to move to Boston with his father and new stepmother.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school. During his tenure, he openly favored sixteen-year-old Prissy Andrews, spending much of his class time seated with her to explain lessons or write verses to her. When Anne Shirley dropped a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after Gilbert called her "carrots," Mr. Phillips made Anne stand on the platform in front of the blackboard and wrote a note above her head about controlling her temper. The next day, after a group of tardy pupils returned late from gum-picking, Mr. Phillips selected Anne as a scapegoat and forced her to sit beside Gilbert Blythe as punishment. Later in the term, he promoted Anne and Gilbert into the fifth class to study advanced branches, praising Anne's rapid progress to Matthew Cuthbert despite her struggles in geometry. At the end of June, his term as teacher concluded and he gave an emotional farewell speech to the students before leaving Avonlea.

When Anne Shirley dropped a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after Gilbert called her "carrots," Mr. Phillips made Anne stand on the platform in front of the blackboard and wrote a note above her head about controlling her temper. The next day, after a group of tardy pupils returned late from gum-picking, Mr. Phillips selected Anne as a scapegoat and forced her to sit beside Gilbert Blythe as punishment. Later in the term, he promoted Anne and Gilbert into the fifth class to study advanced branches, praising Anne's rapid progress to Matthew Cuthbert despite her struggles in geometry. At the end of June, his term as teacher concluded and he gave an emotional farewell speech to the students before leaving Avonlea.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley, joining a close circle of thoughtful and ambitious friends. After graduating, she accepted a teaching position at Carmody School. During her time in the area, she joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and contributed a paper at one of their meetings. In the spring, she went on a memorable woodland outing with Anne, Diana, and Jane. Later, she brought her famous aunt, Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan, to visit Anne at Green Gables. She eventually accepted the teaching position at her home school, leaving Carmody.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived with her meek husband Thomas
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived with her meek husband, Thomas, in Lynde's Hollow on the Avonlea main road. She served as a prominent leader in community organizations, including the Sewing Circle, Sunday School, Church Aid Society, and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert decided to adopt a child, Rachel was astonished and openly doubted the wisdom of bringing an orphan into Green Gables. During her first visit to meet Anne Shirley, Rachel bluntly criticized the girl's looks, prompting Anne to burst into a furious temper, though Rachel readily forgave her when Anne apologized. Over the following years, Rachel frequently offered advice on Anne's upbringing and school affairs, eventually admitting she had been mistaken in her harsh initial judgment as Anne blossomed into a steady and capable girl. Following the death of her husband Thomas after a prolonged illness, Rachel faced financial difficulty due to an unpaid mortgage on her farm. Rather than move away to live with her daughter Eliza outside Avonlea, she accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables and share the house.

value: Ruby attended class under Mr. Phillips as a schoolgirl in Avonlea.
unit: As a schoolgirl in Avonlea, Ruby attended class under Mr. Phillips and frequently shared gossip about suitors and romance. She was a member of the story club created by Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, and she participated in the school concert's tableau and dialogues. Later, she joined Miss Stacy's Queen's preparation class and successfully passed the entrance exams. While attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, she lived in a boarding house and was considered the handsomest girl of her year. After graduating from Queen's with her teaching license, she obtained the position of schoolteacher at Carmody, allowing her to stay connected with her Avonlea friends.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the trustees as the first female teacher at Avonlea school. She introduced novel educational practices, including morning and evening physical culture exercises, nature study field afternoons, composition practice, and biweekly recitation afternoons. In late autumn, she organized a Christmas Night school concert to fund a schoolhouse flag. She later formed an advanced class to prepare willing students for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy, giving them an extra hour of instruction after school. Though offered a job in her home district, she chose to stay in Avonlea for a second year to see her students through their Entrance exams. After successfully guiding all her Queen's class candidates through the examination in Charlottetown, her rule at Avonlea school came to an end at the close of June. She was later invited to dinner at Green Gables alongside the Allans during a visit back to Avonlea.
